articles.title: Home Assistant keeps passwords out of configuration errors
articles.dek: A broad credential check protects logs shared for troubleshooting while retaining the details needed to fix a setting.
body: Home Assistant stops configuration errors from echoing passwords, API keys, access tokens and authentication PINs into logs. A rejected credential is replaced with a redaction marker while the setting’s location and the reason it failed remain visible.

Franck Nijhof applies the protection across hundreds of configuration and setup forms, including 470 password fields and 171 API-key fields. Settings that merely identify something, such as a hardware pin number, stay readable so the error remains useful.

The protection uses the Secret marker in Probatio, the validation engine introduced in Home Assistant 2026.9. Custom integration authors can use that marker for their own credentials; the new developer post explains that existing imports remain compatible.

Mark CONF_API_TOKEN as secret in config flow schemas

Mark CONF_API_KEY as secret in config schemas

articles.title: Home Assistant guides the next steps for multipurpose ESPHome devices
articles.dek: A device checklist connects advertised audio, Bluetooth and radio capabilities to the setup they need.
body: Home Assistant gives compatible ESPHome devices a setup checklist after they are added. A banner leads to the capabilities advertised by the firmware, so a device that can play audio or connect other equipment has a visible next step instead of leaving its owner to find the relevant integration.

Petar Petrov connects the audio path to a Music Assistant offer and enables an available Sendspin switch during setup. Home Assistant systems with Supervisor can install Music Assistant from that flow; other installations receive a Learn more link. Choosing Later leaves a compact reminder on the device page.

Bluetooth proxy support is shown as status, while serial and supported Z-Wave setup hand off to existing Home Assistant flows. Zigbee remains an informational link, and guest access and PIN controls are outside this checklist.

Address review feedback on the ESPHome device setup

articles.title: ESPHome installs Beken firmware from the browser
articles.dek: Device Builder and ESPHome Web gain a USB serial route for BK72xx boards, with browser-based logs.
body: ESPHome extends browser-based firmware installation to Beken BK72xx boards through a USB serial adapter. Device Builder compiles the configuration and sends it to the chip, while ESPHome Web accepts the resulting firmware file. The installer checks that the image matches the connected chip before erasing anything.

J. Nick Koston tested installation on BK7231N and BK7238 hardware. BK7231T and BK7252 support follows the reference protocol and simulated tests, without a physical-board test recorded. A device that does not enter installation mode automatically may need a manual reset.

Browser-based logs join the installer. These chips normally send logs through a different serial connection from the one used for installation, so the adapter’s receive wire needs moving to the logging output afterward. The work extends the Pico and Nordic browser installation paths reported on September 25 to another chip family.

articles.title: Infrared experiments turn learned remotes into Home Assistant integrations
articles.dek: A community proof of concept turns candle and air-conditioner commands into ordinary controls, with broader hardware verification still ahead.
body: David of DAB-LABS reports a working route from capturing an infrared remote to generating a standalone Home Assistant integration. Two proof-of-concept integrations cover Sanmli TH-05 candles and a Daikin FTXS50KVM air conditioner, extending the foundation’s effort to make brand-specific infrared support easier to create.

The Daikin example becomes a normal climate control that sends its full state whenever a setting changes. David says its 521 captured codes cover combinations of mode, fan, swing and temperature, plus Off. The generation tool checks generated codes against captures before producing an integration.

These examples bypassed the planned requirement for several hardware attestations. Wider use still needs that verification, and work continues on air-conditioner protocols and testing without manually pressing hundreds of commands. The public roadmap opportunity remains in Building; these are community prototypes, not a claim of universal remote support.

externalSources.title: Turn any remote into a first-class Home Assistant device

articles.title: AI assistants can inspect and interact with KNX installations
articles.dek: An administrator can attach tools for project information, message history and live bus access.
body: Home Assistant gives configured AI assistants tools for inspecting a KNX building-automation installation and interacting with its control network. The tools reach stored device messages, information from the installation’s ETS project and live KNX access, beyond ordinary Home Assistant entities.

Martin Hoefling connects the tools to Home Assistant conversation agents and to external clients through its Model Context Protocol server. An administrator must first attach the KNX toolset. The set includes tools that transmit on the bus, so it is not a read-only inspection interface.

articles.title: ESPHome gives Zigbee switches an incoming control path
articles.dek: Makers can expose ESP32 switch components over Zigbee, extending the earlier sensor reporting.
body: ESPHome adds Zigbee control of switch components on compatible ESP32 devices. A maker can expose a switch through the standard on-and-off format or a generic binary output, allowing commands from Zigbee to change the component’s state.

Contributor luar123 extends the sensor work reported on September 30 from reporting measurements to receiving control commands. The implementation carries incoming Zigbee changes to ESPHome’s main processing loop; it does not add every kind of controllable component.

articles.title: Music Assistant connects directly to FeiNiu music libraries
articles.dek: An experimental connection brings personal fnOS music collections into Music Assistant without a protocol bridge.
body: Music Assistant adds a direct connection to FeiNiu Music, the personal music-library service for fnOS. A regular FeiNiu account and password provide access to tracks, albums, artists and playlists, alongside search, artwork, lyrics and playback.

The connection is experimental and read-only. Separate instances can use different accounts with their own sign-ins and caches. Contributor neqq3 tested it against FeiNiu Music 1.0.1 (0.8.41) in their first contribution to the Music Assistant server, reviewed by OzGav.

articles.title: Music Assistant starts live BBC programmes from the beginning
articles.dek: The current show joins the station’s schedule as a playable item, with seeking back toward live radio.
body: Music Assistant lets BBC Sounds listeners start the programme currently on air from its beginning. The station’s Today schedule lists that show as playable, using the station’s available rewind window.

Listeners can seek forward to the live broadcast; seeking beyond it returns to live playback. When the programme ends, Music Assistant queues the station’s live stream if nothing else is waiting. Will Wilson makes his first contribution to the Music Assistant server with the addition, reviewed by Marvin Schenkel.

pullRequests.title: Let BBC Sounds rewind the programme on air to its start

articles.title: Home Assistant controls MELCloud Home hot-water tanks
articles.dek: Temperature and priority heating join a clearer account of what the heat pump is doing.
body: MELCloud Home air-to-water systems gain Home Assistant controls for their hot-water tanks. Owners can set a target temperature and choose normal heat-pump operation or forced hot water, which gives the tank priority over the heating zones.

Erwin Douna adds an operation reading that distinguishes idle, water heating, room heating and cooling. Room climate controls also show when the system is actively heating or cooling. Tank controls appear only where the unit reports hot-water support; there is no separate tank power switch because turning off the unit would stop room heating too.

articles.title: Pausing one room no longer blocks music in another
articles.dek: Music Assistant releases an idle stream when another player needs the same service.
body: Music Assistant lets a new player take over a streaming service’s single available stream from a paused player. A voice request that pauses music in the living room and starts it in the kitchen no longer has to wait for the old player’s timeout.

The change covers services with a one-stream limit, including Apple Music, Pandora and Spotify using the Soloist backend. A player that is still playing is never interrupted. The paused player can later resume from its saved position with a new stream, including after it could not be reached to stop the old one.
For players without their own pause support, including Sendspin, Snapcast, Fully Kiosk and speaker groups, pausing releases the source immediately while retaining the place for later playback.

articles.title: Some ESP8266 development builds need a wired recovery
articles.dek: A corrected flash-size setting prevents failed wireless updates on affected custom layouts.
body: An ESPHome development-build fault can leave some ESP8266 devices unable to accept another wireless update or save settings to flash. It affects configurations that override the board’s memory layout with a larger size, including the described Athom configuration.

J. Nick Koston makes the new native build system write a matching size into the firmware header. A device already running the broken development image needs one serial reinstallation; a device still using firmware built with PlatformIO can update wirelessly to a corrected build. Ordinary board layouts are unchanged.

pullRequests.title: [esp8266] Derive the native image header flash size from the linker script

articles.title: Home Assistant flags commands that depend on templated shell features
articles.dek: A six-month transition warns owners before a stricter command execution rule takes effect.
body: Home Assistant starts a six-month transition away from running templated Command line commands through a shell. Configurations that combine templates with shell features receive a repair notice, while the existing shell behavior continues during the transition.
Martin Hjelmare brings the integration closer to Shell Command’s security approach. A follow-up preserves a person’s decision to ignore the repair notice instead of repeatedly recreating it.

articles.title: Home Assistant starts complete Rain Bird watering programs
articles.dek: Automations can reuse the controller’s saved zones and run times.
body: Rain Bird owners gain a Home Assistant button for each watering program supported by their controller. Starting a program uses the zones and run times already saved on the controller, instead of recreating the sequence by starting individual zones.
Pavan tested the buttons on an ESP-TM2, checking that each program starts and that the zone switches reflect it. Joost Lek reviewed the work.

articles.title: Music Assistant avoids starting Smart Fades on smaller hosts
articles.dek: Automatic setup requires more memory and processor capacity; manual setup keeps its existing minimum.
body: Music Assistant stops automatically enabling Smart Fades on a first startup unless the host meets its recommended six-gigabyte, four-core specification. Loading the feature’s audio-analysis software on a shared four-gigabyte Home Assistant machine risks exhausting memory and causing the operating system to terminate a process.

Marvin Schenkel keeps the lower four-gigabyte, two-core minimum for people who deliberately enable the feature themselves. Existing manual choices remain manual; the stricter requirement applies to automatic first-time setup.
